headline: Red Sox trade Early for Mead as bats go cold in loss
morning_brew: What the hell was that at Fenway? Getting shut down to one hit in a six-run loss is exactly the kind of disastah that ruins your weekend before it even starts. Sonny Gray had a brutal night on the mound, giving up five earned runs in five innings, and the offense could not buy a run to save their lives. It was one of those games where I watched the whole thing through my fingers like a horror movie, wondering if these guys were actually taking batting practice or just standing out there for the fresh air.

While the game was a total wash, the front office was busy moving pieces, shipping Connelly Early off to the Nationals to bring in infielder Curtis Mead. It is a classic swap of young talent, and honestly, if it brings a little more life to the infield, I am all for it. We need a shake-up, and seeing the front office pull the trigger on a deal like this signals they are not ready to just roll over and fold up shop for the season. It is a small deposit in the Duck Boat fund, for now.

We have a quick turnaround today with a day game against the Blue Jays before we ship out to California. I really hope the guys can wake up and put that embarrassment behind them because this team is better than what we saw last night. My neighbor Rick is already drafting a letter to the front office about the bullpen rotation, and honestly, after watching the arson squad last night, I am not even gonna try to talk him out of it. He is on day two of his umpire-and-pitching dossier, and I fear he has finally lost it.

news_digest.headline: Red Sox trade LHP Connelly Early to Nationals for Curtis Mead
news_digest.dans_take: Trading for Mead is an interesting swing for the fences; about damn time we saw some movement to help the offense.
